core_job: A personal health record on the phone for adults managing ongoing care (several medicines, a condition checked at visits, several clinicians). It keeps medicines with their history, readings, lab results, symptoms, sleep, activity, workouts and a food diary on one searchable timeline, plus your clinicians (CMS NPPES) and your visits. There is no account and nothing is uploaded.
signature:
The "Since last visit" brief. Pick a clinician and MyHealth builds a one-page brief of what changed since your last logged visit with them:
- medicines started, stopped or changed in dose, with dates (from a new change log; RxNorm ingredient names)
- adherence from your own dose logs
- stats for each reading type
- lab results against the range printed on your report, with the previous value
- the symptoms you logged
- a sleep and activity summary
- live openFDA recall reports for your ingredients, where HTTP 404 means "none" and offline means "not run"
- your questions

Each section can be switched off. Output is an on-screen preview, a PDF through the share sheet, or copied text. "Log this visit" starts the next window.

Competitors were checked with the keyless iTunes Lookup API, because web search is disabled in this session. Guava already advertises "Doctor Visit Prep" and Medisafe a PDF report, so the gap claimed is narrower: a per-clinician view of what changed since the last visit, plus recall checks, with no account and no uploads. That gap rests on store descriptions only.

Every API used was curl-verified today. RxNav's drug-interaction API returned 404, so it is excluded.
